text: an empty inbox
to spend less time planning dinners
noticing you've had pasta twice this week already
not spending an hour choosing a movie
tomorrow fully planned before you wake up
to never forget an umbrella again
never forgetting a commitment
a nudge about that errand — right when you're passing the place
birthdays remembered a week early
birthdays remembered with a gift idea
the passport checked before the airport
the subscriptions you forgot you pay for
cancelling a subscription without the phone call
the insurance that quietly got pricier, caught
the bills paid before the reminder
the newsletters read for you
the news, without the doomscroll
what's on this weekend — without opening five apps
every "oh, I should…" caught before it evaporates
"let's grab coffee" actually becoming coffee
the form due in March done in February
the car booked before the warning light does it
the kids' schedule out of your head
not being the family's IT department
every warranty and receipt findable
"you sound stressed — here's the short version"
the doctor's appointment actually booked
the fridge emptied before things go off
the packing list ready a week before the trip
the gift bought before the party, not on the way
a workout that fits today's calendar
knowing which of your friends you've gone quiet on
the tax stuff gathered in one place, in January
the recipe scaled for four, and the shopping list to match
the parking ticket paid before it doubles
a clean, prioritised inbox
meeting notes sent before you're back at your desk
"you promised Kari a document. It's Thursday."
timesheets filled from your calendar
Friday afternoon back
14 Slack channels caught up in two minutes
"you've been asked this three times — here's a doc"
who that person is, before they say hello
the client brief in your pocket before the room
what you decided in March — and why
the follow-up you keep not sending, sent
the 60-page report, briefed against your questions
the status update written from what you actually did
data entry that enters itself
the documents filed where you'll actually find them
a meeting that could've been an email — flagged before you accept
the expense report done from the receipts in your inbox
the travel booked, the way you like to travel
your week's priorities, in one line, Monday 8am
the person you keep meaning to thank, thanked
a second pair of eyes at midnight
the spacing slips caught before the review
handoff notes drafted from the file
the build drifting from the design — noticed before the developer does
stakeholder feedback from six threads, one honest list
"make the logo bigger," translated
"the design system already has that"
your rationale saved, so you don't re-argue it
every reference you've ever saved, findable by vibe
the case study drafted while the work is still fresh
contrast checked on every screen, every time
the copy made consistent across 40 screens
user interview notes turned into themes overnight
the PR reviewing itself first
"almost right" AI code caught before it costs the afternoon
the 30 minutes a day of hunting for answers, back
to know what's new in the project since you last touched it
"you've been rubber-ducking this for 40 minutes"
dependency updates triaged: three matter, twelve don't
which of the 200 CI failures is yours
someone who knows why the codebase looks like that
the changelog written from the commits — properly
the on-call handover written before you're off
the ticket updated without opening Jira
"who owns this service?" answered before you ask in Slack
the tech-debt list everyone knows about, actually written down
the flaky test named and shamed
the release notes your PM can actually read
the environment that just works on Monday
to walk into every meeting fully briefed
the school messages, Spond and the family calendar turned into one plan
the plan updated when the fourth message of the day changes it
the birthday party flagged a week early — not the morning of
standing appointments accepted for you — unless something clashes
travel times already in the plan
the kids to have their own copy of the plan
to spend less time planning something so small
to be told to get up and go for a run
to be reminded you own a ukulele
more board games with the kids
time to draw again
your two strength sessions actually happening
time to do nothing — scheduled
your team’s CVs kept up to date without asking
incoming sales matched with who’s actually free
what’s bubbling in your field summarised, the good stuff saved
a ping when the industry you’re chasing gets a new marketing chief
to search everything said in the leadership meetings
to know who’s on which project right now
to stop keeping track of who merged with whom
the Slack channel where people only post links — explained
your handbook to answer the questions people keep asking
your deep-work time actually protected
to never miss your favourite band in town again
dinner ideas from what's actually in the fridge
